- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk reversal.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (e.g., 70+), especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct — apply upward bias to counteract.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to be too optimistic in early days (e.g., day 1–3) — dampen initial forecast values.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +1.00 to -0.33), model reacts too slowly — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment shift.
